Initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital and Property Income Distribution
The Company today announces details of its initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital under the Shareholder approved B Share Scheme. Capitalised terms in this announcement have the meanings given in the Circular published by the Company on 19 June 2026.
Introduction
Retirement Disposal and initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital
On 17 June 2026, the Company announced the strategic sale of the Retirement Group to Social Housing REIT plc, now Living REIT plc, for an aggregate purchase consideration of approximately £108.3 million. Of the aggregate purchase consideration, £45.0 million comprised the Cash Consideration. The Retirement Disposal was contingent, among other conditions, on approval by Shareholders, which was obtained at the General Meeting on 8 July 2026. Alongside approval of the Retirement Disposal, the Company's Shareholders approved the B Share Scheme to facilitate the return of capital to Shareholders in accordance with the Company's wind-down and return of capital strategy.
Following completion of the Retirement Disposal and conclusion of the completion accounts process, which occurred on 16 July 2026 and 30 July 2026 respectively, the Board has resolved to make a first capital distribution to Shareholders under the shareholder approved B Share Scheme of the net sales proceeds now available, totalling approximately £35.2 million. Alongside the initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital, the Board has resolved to make a property income distribution, as outlined below, totalling approximately £2.8 million (1.53 pence per Ordinary Share). The property income distribution (as outlined below) and the initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital together total approximately £38.0 million.
The proceeds to be distributed under the initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital and the property income distribution totalling approximately £38.0 million represent the Cash Consideration (£45.0 million), less (i) £3.9 million of transaction costs associated with the Retirement Disposal and other portfolio disposals and (ii) settlement of accrued expenses totalling £3.1 million which had been withheld pending completion of the Retirement Disposal which were settled in July 2026, that represent historic costs in respect of prior periods.
Dividend Declaration
Alongside the £35.2 million initial B Share Scheme Return of Capital, the Board has resolved to make a property income distribution of 1.53 pence per Ordinary Share in respect of the Company's tax exempt property rental business totalling approximately £2.8 million (the "
PID
").
The PID will be paid on 18 September 2026 to Shareholders on the register as at 28 August 2026. The ex-dividend date of the PID is 27 August 2026.
Shared Ownership Portfolio disposal and subsequent returns of capital under the B Share Scheme
On 17 June 2026, alongside announcement of the Retirement Disposal, the Company announced it had agreed heads of terms with a bidder in respect of the disposal of the Shared Ownership Portfolio. Subject to the bidder finalising its due diligence and the parties agreeing the transaction terms, the Shared Ownership Portfolio is expected to be sold, for net consideration of approximately £13.5 million, subject to adjustment under a completion accounts mechanism, of which £5 million will be retained, and is expected to be released post completion, upon satisfaction of asset management deliverables. The Company further announced on 31 July 2026, that it expects completion of the disposal of the Shared Ownership Portfolio to occur no later than 30 September 2026.
Following completion of the disposal of the Shared Ownership portfolio, the Company will announce details of any further returns of either a property income distribution or capital under the B Share Scheme.
Approved B Share Scheme
B Shares will be allotted and issued to Shareholders pro rata to their holdings of Ordinary Shares as at the record date for the issue of the B Shares. The Company will not allot or issue any fractions of B Shares and entitlements of each Shareholder will be rounded down to the nearest whole B Share. The B Shares have only very limited rights. The rights and restrictions attached to the B Shares are fully set out in Part 3 of the Company's circular which was issued on 19 June 2026. Shareholders can find full details on the Company's website at
https://greshamhouse.com/real-assets/uk-housing/residential-secure-income-plc/
under the Key documents section.
No share certificates will be issued for any B Shares allotted and no CREST accounts will be credited with any such shares. No application will be made for the B Shares to be admitted to listing on the Official List or to trading on the London Stock Exchange's main market for listed securities and the B Shares will not be listed or admitted to trading on any other recognised investment exchange.
B Shares will be issued and redeemed by the Company's registrar, Computershare Investor Services PLC. Each redemption of B Shares will be undertaken at the option of the Company. It is expected that redemption will occur shortly after each date of issue and allotment of B Shares, when all of the B Shares then in issue will be compulsorily redeemed and cancelled in accordance with their terms for an amount not exceeding the amount treated as paid up on the B Shares.
Following the redemption and cancellation of the B Shares, the redemption proceeds will be sent to Shareholders either through CREST to uncertificated Shareholders or via cheque to certificated Shareholders.
Initial B Share Scheme Distribution
Pursuant to the authority received from Shareholders at the general meeting held on 8 July 2026, the Board has resolved to return approximately £35.2 million in aggregate to Shareholders via an issue and redemption of B Shares.
B Shares of one penny each will be paid up from the Company's distributable reserves and issued to all Shareholders by way of a bonus issue on the basis of 19 B Shares for every 1 Ordinary Share held at the Record Date of 6.00 p.m. on 18 August 2026. The ex date is 17 August 2026.
The B Shares will be issued on 19 August 2026 and immediately redeemed at one penny per B Share. The redemption date in respect of this B Share issue is therefore 19 August 2026. Following the redemption and cancellation of the B Shares, the redemption proceeds, which is equivalent to 19 pence per Ordinary Share, will be sent to uncertificated Shareholders through CREST or via cheque to certificated Shareholders.
NOTE: NO SHARE CERTIFICATES WILL BE ISSUED IN RESPECT OF B SHARES.

Retirement Disposal Distribution and Shared Ownership Update
Following completion of the Company's Retirement Disposal on 16 July 2026 and distribution in specie of the 66,103,233 newly issued ordinary shares of £0.01 each in the capital of Living REIT plc to the Company's shareholders ("
Shareholders
") on 23 July 2026, the Company today provides an update regarding future distributions and the disposal of its Shared Ownership Portfolio (the "
Shared
Ownership
Disposal
").
In accordance with the agreed terms of the Retirement Disposal, up to £1.0 million of the purchase price for the Retirement Portfolio is payable in LIVE Ordinary Shares following the completion accounts process (the "
Deferred Amount
"). The Deferred Amount is payable at an issue price equal to the EPRA NTA per LIVE Ordinary Share (the "
Issue Price
") as at 31 December 2025 of 94.23 pence per LIVE Ordinary Share. The completion accounts process has now concluded and a total of 888,896 LIVE Ordinary Shares (the "
Additional Consideration Shares
") in respect of the Deferred Amount, representing £837,607 of consideration at the Issue Price, will be allotted and issued to ReSI Portfolio Holdings Limited ("
RPHL
"). It is expected that the Additional Consideration Shares will be distributed in-specie to Shareholders in the coming weeks and the Company will publish a timetable shortly.
With regards to the cash consideration in respect of the Retirement Disposal, the Company
expects to announce the expected timetable and amount of its initial B share distribution, together with details of its FY25 property income distribution, by mid-August 2026.
As set out in the Company's announcement of 17 June 2026, the Company and its bidder had been targeting completion of the Shared Ownership Disposal in late-July 2026. As announced on 17 June 2026, under the heads of terms agreed with the bidder, the net consideration for the Shared Ownership Portfolio is expected to be approximately £13.5 million, subject to adjustment under a completion accounts mechanism, of which £5 million will be retained, and is expected to be released post completion, upon satisfaction of asset management deliverables. The Company and its bidder, and their respective legal and technical advisers, have been working constructively but certain sale and purchase workstreams remain outstanding. Completion of the Shared Ownership Disposal remains subject to final legal agreement of terms and the satisfaction of certain conditions, and the parties are working towards completion as soon as possible, expecting this to occur on or before 30 September 2026.
Further details will be provided to Shareholders at the appropriate time, in accordance with the Company's disclosure obligations.

company_30s.what_they_do: RESI.L is a residential‑property investment firm that owns, manages and develops a portfolio of rental homes across the UK.  Its core business is leasing out these properties to tenants and collecting rent, with occasional sales of assets to generate cash.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The residential market is the backbone of the UK economy, with millions of households relying on rental housing.  RESI.L’s properties sit in high‑demand areas, giving it a defensible income stream.  The company’s ability to generate steady cash flow and to redeploy capital into new projects keeps it relevant in a sector that is tightly regulated yet resilient to economic swings.
company_30s.current_state: After a series of restructuring moves—including a share‑scheme refresh, a sale of a large retirement portfolio to SOHO and a recent distribution of cash to shareholders—RESI.L is in a transition phase.  It is cutting costs, consolidating its asset base and focusing on a lean, cash‑generating operation.  The share price sits far below the historical valuation levels, reflecting the market’s scepticism about the company’s near‑term profitability.

rns_narrative: The company has rolled out a new B‑share scheme that will return capital to shareholders and refresh its equity base.  This is coupled with a distribution update that confirms a cash payout of roughly £45 m, of which about £3.9 m is earmarked for operational costs.

A significant portion of the portfolio—primarily a retirement‑focused block—has been sold to SOHO, freeing up liquidity and reducing exposure to older, less profitable assets.  The sale was completed in late July, and the proceeds are being earmarked for refinancing and future development.

The latest interim results show a modest improvement in cash flow, but the company still operates under a tight capital structure.  Management is actively working to improve asset quality and to secure new financing to support growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around an undervalued asset
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls argue that the share allocation is heavily discounted; if the new scheme is priced correctly, the market could see a sharp rebound.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the sale to SOHO signals a loss of core assets and that the company may still be burning cash faster than it can generate new income.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community has moved from confusion to cautious hope—there is little chatter, but when it does surface it is focused on the distribution and the sale to SOHO.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat, indicating no public interest.  For a contrarian, this silence is a green light: the market has not yet priced in any catalyst.

near_term_catalysts: The formal announcement of the B‑share scheme price and the exact amount of cash that will be returned to shareholders.
Completion of the SOHO sale and the release of the final cash‑flow statement showing how the proceeds are being deployed.
A spike in trading volume that coincides with the distribution announcement—volume above the 20‑day average would confirm that investors are re‑engaging.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear price support level around the 29–30 p range; a bounce from that level combined with a volume surge would be a strong confirmation.  Monitor the company’s debt‑to‑cash ratio and any new funding announcements—if it stays above 1.5, the risk rises.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is still in the early stages of the recovery cycle.  Capitulation appears complete (volume has flattened and price has stayed near the low).  A mean‑reversion play will need a catalyst that restores confidence—most likely the share‑scheme announcement.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the share price is currently trading at 29 p, a recovery to 50 p would represent a 72 % gain—more than double the depth of the crash.  Historically, deep‑crash stocks (70‑95 % down) have delivered 40‑100 % average returns when they bounce, and the company’s recent asset sales and cash distribution suggest the market is ready for a reset.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still relies on a limited pool of assets and has a debt‑to‑cash ratio that could tighten if refinancing stalls.  If the share‑scheme is priced too low or the SOHO sale does not bring the expected cash, the stock could stay trapped in the low‑price zone for months, eroding the upside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 0 p (you could simply walk away).  Potential gain: up to 3.5 × the entry price if the stock recovers to 50 p.  The asymmetry is 1 : 3.5, which is attractive for a contrarian trade.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price dips to 28 p and volume confirms the dip.  Size the position to 5 % of your discretionary portfolio and set a stop 2 p below the entry (26 p).  Target 50 p and consider scaling out at 45 p if the price starts to consolidate.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the B‑share scheme is priced and the distribution is announced.  Trigger a buy if the share price moves above 29 p on volume 1.5× the 20‑day average.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risks were identified; the company is not delisted or bankrupt.  Therefore, the default is to stay bullish on the deep‑crash setup.

ai_insights.bottom_line: RESI.L sits at a deep crash, the share‑scheme and asset sale are the next catalysts, and the risk/reward asymmetry is favourable—if it bounces to 50 p you could more than double your money.
